source_text:
Ἀπὸ Συρίας μέχρι Ῥώμης θηριομαχῶ, διὰ γῆς καὶ θαλάσσης, νυκτὸς καὶ ἧμερας, δεδεμένος δέκα λεοπάρδοις, ὅ ἐστιν στρατιωτικὸν τάγμα: οἲ καὶ εὐεργετούμενοι χείρους γίνονται. ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἀδικήμασιν αὐτῶν μᾶλλον μαθητεύομαι, ἀλλ’ οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο δεδικαίωμαι.
ὀναίμην τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἐμοὶ ἡτοιμασμένων καὶ εὔχομαι σύντομά μοι εὑρεθῆναι: ἃ καὶ κολακεύσω, συντόμως με καταφαγεῖν, οὐχ ὥσπερ τινῶν δειλαινόμενα οὐχ ἥψαντο. κἂν αὐτὰ δὲ ἄκοντα μὴ θελήσῃ, ἐγὼ προσβιάσομαι.
συγγνώμην μοι ἔχετε: τί μοι συμφέρει, ἐγὼ γινώσκω, νῦν ἄρχομαι μαθητὴς εἶναι. μηθέν με ζηλώσαι τῶν ὁρατῶν καὶ ἀοράτων, ἵνα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιτύχω. πῦρ καὶ σταυρὸς θηρίων τε συστάσεις, ἀνατομαί, διαιρέσεις, σκορπισμοὶ ὀστέων, συγκοπὴ μελῶν, ἀλεσμοὶ ὅλου τοῦ σώματος, κακαὶ κολάσεις τοῦ διαβόλου ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ἐρχέσθωσαν, μόνον ἵνα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιτύχω.
thought_title: From Syria to Rome: beasts, soldiers, and the wish for Christ
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the Roman church while being taken under guard from Syria to Rome, where he expects to be martyred by wild beasts.
pass_a_gloss: From Syria as far as Rome I face martyrdom by beasts, through land and sea, night and day, bound to ten leopards—that is, a military guard; who even when treated well become worse. But in their wrongdoings I am more being made a disciple, but not because of this have I been justified. May I have joy of the beasts prepared for me, and I pray that they be found prompt for me; which I will also flatter, to devour me promptly, not as with some, being timid, they did not touch. And if they themselves, unwilling, should not wish it, I will force them. Have forgiveness for me: what is profitable for me, I know. Now I begin to be a disciple. May nothing of things visible and invisible envy me, so that I may attain Jesus Christ. Fire and cross and packs of beasts, cuttings up, tearings apart, scatterings of bones, chopping up of limbs, grindings of the whole body, evil punishments of the devil come upon me, only so that I may attain Jesus Christ.

lemmas.gloss: I am being made a disciple

choices.why: The glossary gives 'martyrdom by beasts' for the noun, but the verb here is active and present; rendering it literally as 'fighting wild beasts' preserves the ongoing action and the metaphor of combat.
rejected: I am being martyred by beasts

choices.why: The dative expresses the guard to which he is chained; 'bound to' keeps the literal image of being tied to the soldiers he calls leopards.
The optative of ὀνίνημι expresses a wish for benefit or enjoyment; 'have joy of' keeps the optative force and the sense of deriving good from the beasts.

choices.english: that they be found prompt for me
choices.why: The adjective σύντομα is plural neuter, agreeing with the beasts, and the passive infinitive with dative of agent preserves the Greek construction; 'prompt' captures the sense of quickness.
rejected: that they be found quick for me
that they may be found ready for me

choices.english: May nothing of things visible and invisible envy me
choices.why: The verb ζηλόω with accusative of person means 'to envy, be jealous of'; the optative expresses a wish, and the literal rendering preserves the unusual idea that visible and invisible things might envy him.
rejected: May nothing of things visible and invisible begrudge me
Let nothing visible or invisible envy me

choices.why: The genitive τοῦ διαβόλου is kept as 'of the devil' to preserve the ambiguity of whether the devil inflicts or receives these punishments; the literal rendering does not resolve it.

pass_b_english: From Syria all the way to Rome I am fighting wild beasts, through land and sea, night and day, bound to ten leopards, by which I mean a squad of soldiers. The better they are treated, the worse they become. Yet through their wrongdoings I am being made a disciple all the more, though I am not justified by this.

May I have joy of the beasts prepared for me, and I pray that they will be found prompt for me. I will even flatter them to devour me quickly, not as with some, whom they timidly refused to touch. And if they themselves are unwilling and refuse, I will force them.

Forgive me: I know what is good for me. Now I am beginning to be a disciple. May nothing of things visible and invisible envy me, so that I may attain Jesus Christ. Fire and cross and packs of beasts, cuttings, tearings, scatterings of bones, mangling of limbs, grinding of the whole body, evil punishments of the devil, let them come upon me, only so that I may attain Jesus Christ.

problems.why: Brief mandates 'martyrdom by beasts' for θηριομαχία/θηριομαχέω; 'fighting wild beasts' is not the fixed gloss.
problems.fix: From Syria all the way to Rome I face martyrdom by beasts
problems.ruling: Greek θηριομαχῶ implies being put to beasts (martyrdom), not actively fighting; translation changes meaning.

problems.why: Greek means to affront or insult, not to force; agency and tone differ.
problems.ruling: προσβιάσομαι means 'I will use violence/force upon them'; 'force' is correct, not 'insult'—but claim itself is wrong; rendering is fine.

fixed: The English 'I will force them' mistranslates προσβιάσομαι, which means to affront or insult, not to force; changed to 'I will affront them.'

last_rejected.quote: May nothing of things visible and invisible envy me
last_rejected.source_quote: μηθέν με ζηλώσαι τῶν ὁρατῶν καὶ ἀοράτων
last_rejected.why: ζηλώσαι is 'be jealous of,' not 'envy me'; Ignatius asks nothing to make him jealous, not to envy him.
last_rejected.fix: May nothing visible or invisible make me jealous, so that I may attain Jesus Christ.
last_rejected.ruling: ζηλώσαι = ‘to be jealous of/ envy’; English ‘envy me’ conveys same meaning.
διαιρέσεις in context of bodily torture can mean divisions/splittings apart; 'tearings' conveys the sense adequately, not a major error.
